input: s is an ASCII binary string of length L with 0 <= L <= 1000; n is an integer in [1,1000000000]. Empty s is an explicit extension. Integer inputs are plain int values excluding bool. Containers are ordinary lists and strings are ordinary str values, without subclasses or overloaded behavior. No concurrent mutation or modified standard built-ins are allowed. Preconditions are not dynamically validated. Size bounds do not guarantee available memory or completion within an unqualified runtime budget.
return: A Boolean indicating whether the canonical binary representation of every integer from 1 through n occurs as a contiguous substring of s. Leading zeroes in s are allowed but are not part of a positive integer canonical representation.
mutation_aliasing: The input string and scalar n are unchanged. A private set records only distinct positive substring values no larger than n; no caller state is retained. The Solution instance retains no state; separate calls share no mutable result state.
numeric: Only substrings beginning with 1 are expanded. Before each append the value is at most n, so the evaluated value*2+bit is at most 2*n+1 <= 2000000001; expansion stops immediately when it exceeds n. All values and set-size comparisons remain exact safe integers. There is no loop over all integers up to n.
complexity: Let B be the binary length of n, at most 30. O(L*min(L,B+1)+1) expected time and O(min(n,L*B)+1) set storage, including every substring step and insertion. Starting at 1 forces a value beyond n after at most B+1 bits. A set of n distinct values from [1,n] is exactly the required full set. Map/set costs assume ordinary average O(1) operations after charging key construction/hash/comparison; no universal ECMAScript constant-time or adversarial collision-resistance guarantee is claimed.
